question: Can a conservative two-dimensional Green kernel whose drift and anisotropy are derived only from the baryonic field improve cluster-lensing morphology while remaining screened in the Solar System and controlled on galaxy rotation curves?

field_operator.source: observed baryonic member positions and F160W weights
field_operator.tidal_axis: e_i is the principal eigenvector of the softened Hessian generated by every other baryonic source
field_operator.photon_closure: nabla^2 psi=2*kappa_route; alpha=gradient(psi), giving a curl-free deflection field
field_operator.conservation: every source kernel is normalized; no independent dark component is inserted

cluster_data.target_warning: All ten systems and both reconstruction methods are spent data from earlier stages. Cross-validation protects whole systems but is exploratory, not fresh confirmation.

cluster_validation.assignment: sort systems by SHA256 label and round-robin; two systems held per fold
cluster_validation.selection: minimum equal-system Lenstool training Jensen-Shannon divergence among tensor candidates

galaxy_data.completion: fixed RAR applied after conservative radial projection of the selected tensor kernel

claim_limits: The cluster targets are model-dependent convergence reconstructions, not raw image or shear likelihoods.
F160W member light omits a same-resolution gas map and uses luminosity as a baryonic source proxy.
The tensor kernel is a phenomenological Green function, not yet derived from a covariant action.
The radial galaxy projection is an axisymmetric closure of the two-dimensional kernel, not an exact disk calculation.
All ten cluster maps are spent; any selected tensor law requires a different raw cluster for confirmation.
